title: Trump's tiger posts
ticker: Trump posts video of fatal tiger attack in England, then an AI video of himself with a tiger
Victim's family: the footage is causing "severe distress" - please stop sharing it
Piers Morgan: "Appallingly tasteless. Delete it, President Trump"
White House refers questions to the posts themselves

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: President Trump is facing a wave of criticism over a string of *strange posts* on his social media account.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: He shared real footage of a man being *attacked by a tiger* at a British wildlife park, a man who later died.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Hours later, he posted an *AI video* of himself playing with a tiger.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The man's family had begged the public *not to share* the footage.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: A note before we begin. We will *not show* the attack in this report.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It happened on Tuesday, October thirteenth, in *three posts*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: First, a 41-second video from *Yorkshire Wildlife Park* in England, appearing to show a tiger attacking a man inside its enclosure.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He shared it with his roughly *13 million followers* on Truth Social. The White House's *Rapid Response* account also posted it on X.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Minutes later, a second video. A *24-second montage* of big cats attacking people, set to music, with no caption.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: News outlets said it was not clear whether all of that footage was *real*, or partly made with AI.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Then, late that night, the third post. An *AI-generated video* of Trump himself with a tiger.

scenes.name: Donald J. Trump
scenes.post: Don't ever mess with nature! President DJT

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The caption on the first video read: *Don't ever mess with nature!* President DJT.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: That was the only explanation he gave.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: When reporters asked the White House why the president shared it, the White House simply *referred them to the posts*.

scenes.name: Donald J. Trump
scenes.post: [AI video: Trump points at a tiger, then wrestles and hugs it. Music: "The Lion Sleeps Tonight"]

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The AI video shows Trump on a lawn, pointing at a tiger, then *wrestling and hugging* the animal.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The soundtrack: the 1961 hit *The Lion Sleeps Tonight*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Fact-checkers at *Snopes* confirmed Trump really posted it.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: They noted the AI Trump *copies a hand gesture* the man made during the real attack.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The man in that first video was a real person, and his family is *grieving*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Police identified him as *William Chapman*, 23, a former child actor who appeared on British television.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Saturday, October tenth, he entered a tiger enclosure at the park and suffered *fatal injuries*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Witnesses said he had climbed down from a raised walkway. Some visitors tried to *distract the tiger*, without success.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The tiger, a 420-pound Amur tiger named *Altai*, was not hurt. The park says it will *not* be put down.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The park stayed *closed* for days, and the local council has opened a *health and safety investigation*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Police had asked the public *not to share* any footage of the incident.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A former government zoo adviser said that, despite the best security, a *determined person* can sometimes get into an enclosure.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Visitors have left *flowers* at the park entrance, and an inquest into his death is due to open at Doncaster coroner's court.

scenes.name: William Chapman's family
scenes.quote: The publication and circulation of deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress at an exceptionally vulnerable time. We ask people to stop doing this.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On the same day Trump posted, the family released a statement.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: They said they were *utterly devastated*, and described William as a *bright, warm and engaging* young man who had suffered from significant mental illness.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The circulation of deeply offensive media content, they said, is causing *severe distress* at an exceptionally vulnerable time.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *We ask people to stop doing this.*

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: His old stage school paid tribute too, saying he will be *truly missed* and remembered with great fondness.

scenes.name: Oliver Coppard
scenes.quote: The president of the United States now using AI to mock that incident... should be greeted with the contempt it deserves.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Local leaders in England were furious. South Yorkshire's mayor, *Oliver Coppard*, said the family had contacted his office about the pain the videos were causing.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The president of the United States, he said, is now *using AI to mock* the incident, for little more than a cheap laugh on social media.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It should be greeted, he said, with *the contempt it deserves*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Downing Street said people should *respect the family's wishes*, but would not comment on the president's posts, saying he has a press secretary for that.

scenes.name: Will Travers
scenes.quote: Not only incredibly insensitive... It increases the risk to the lives of humans and captive wild animals.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Animal welfare groups were also alarmed by the *AI video*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *Will Travers* of the Born Free Foundation called it not only incredibly insensitive, but *reckless*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Such videos, he warned, can encourage people to seek *direct, high-risk contact* with captive wild animals.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The reaction online was swift, and it came even from *Trump's friends*.

scenes.name: Piers Morgan
scenes.quote: This is appallingly tasteless. Delete it, President @realDonaldTrump.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: British broadcaster *Piers Morgan*, who won Trump's Celebrity Apprentice in 2008 and has known him for nearly two decades, was blunt.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *This is appallingly tasteless*, he wrote. *Delete it*, President Trump.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: His post was viewed more than *1.7 million* times.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Former federal prosecutor *Ron Filipkowski* wondered if the account had been *hacked*, or if a White House aide was sending some kind of message.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Vanity Fair's Washington correspondent said the president was posting *lion snuff films*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Lawyer *Aaron Parnas* called it bizarre and *concerning behavior*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Under the White House's own post on X, many commenters called it *disgusting* and *disrespectful* to the man who died.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Not everyone was critical.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *Ryan Fournier*, founder of Students for Trump, said the president was sending a *clear message*. Don't mess with nature.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: When you cross boundaries with wild animals, he wrote, *nature wins every time*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But even some supporters pushed back. *I voted for you, but not for this*, one commenter wrote under the White House post.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: For many observers, this was not a one-off, but part of a *long pattern* in how the president uses social media.

items.text: AI video of Gaza as a luxury resort
AI "King Trump" video dumping sludge on protesters

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: This is not the first time Trump's posts have raised eyebrows.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In early 2025, he shared an *AI-generated vision of Gaza* rebuilt as a luxury resort, complete with a giant golden statue of himself.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Later that year, after nationwide *No Kings* protests, he posted an AI video of himself as *King Trump*, flying a jet and dumping brown sludge on protesters.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also shared an apparent AI video promoting so-called *MedBed* hospitals, a long-running online conspiracy theory, before it was taken down.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He once posted an image of himself as *Jesus Christ*, and deleted it after criticism from religious groups.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And critics point out he has attacked people *after their deaths* before, including Senator *John McCain*, Congressman *John Dingell*, and director *Rob Reiner*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Fact-checkers at Snopes now keep a running list of *things Trump really posted*, because so many sound too strange to be true.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: One researcher calls the White House's use of AI memes *memetic warfare*, where anyone offended is cast as someone who simply *can't take a joke*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So far, the White House has *not explained* why the president shared the videos.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: A grieving family asked the public to stop sharing their son's final moments. That *same day*, the president of the United States shared them with his followers.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: If you found this helpful, please *like and subscribe* for more.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching.
